endorsements.quote: With the introduction of AI, the main challenge that arises naturally is to develop a well-defined protocol of liability and involvement in case the patient is mistreated on the basis of an inaccurate analysis conducted by the AI (Makary and Daniel, 2016 ).
This refers to the AI sub-systems having enough documented processes and retrievable raw data needed to assess its overall performance.

Indeed, data collection has to be as broadly inclusive as possible, taking into consideration age, race, and gender of patients, and reducing the bias toward under-represented patient groups, whose data might not have been taken into account in earlier AI integration stages (Tahri Sqalli et al., 2021b ).

unlisted_practices: Develop socially-situated explainable AI by incorporating social transparency (descriptive, procedural, and substantive) into AI systems.
Continuously test AI algorithms and implement more robust data collection strategies.
Continuously audit AI systems operating within hospitals.
Closely monitor edge cases for individual patients and investigate how the AI arrived at erroneous outputs.
Design AI systems in medical training to give feedback and support tailored to individual trainees' needs regardless of background or prior experience.
Design AI training models to account for trainees' disadvantaged backgrounds to promote equitable medical training outcomes.
Enable identification of misbehaving AI actors or subsystems and separation of AI recommendations from human clinician decisions.
Enable identification of root causes behind an AI system's decisions or outputs.
Foster interdisciplinary collaboration among patients, clinicians, data scientists, educators, developers, and policymakers in AI design and deployment.
Provide digital health literacy training for healthcare professionals.
Educators should develop inter-professional learning opportunities to identify data biases, bioethical difficulties, and liability risks in AI use.
Policymakers should create regulations and standards that promote social transparency in AI systems.
Develop standards and best practices for AI-based medical training systems.
Develop tools and methods for explaining AI system function to non-experts.

screen.reason: This is a perspective article presenting an ethical framework with recommendations for designing and deploying AI systems in medical training.
